discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-atom-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller (with Jaksch) proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters. Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition in 2002, turning Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a working laboratory. That result made optical lattices the standard platform for studying strongly correlated matter. Greiner and Bloch then developed quantum gas microscopes, which image individual atoms and spins in a many-body state one lattice site at a time. With them the field has observed antiferromagnetic order in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, many-body localization and the dynamics of entanglement. These experiments show many-body phenomena in real space at the level of single particles, and they affect condensed matter, quantum information and high-energy physics. The resulting paradigm (a clean model Hamiltonian, full control and single-particle readout) now shapes quantum science across disciplines.
